meta.name: San Francisco (downtown and the northern waterfront)
meta.scaleNote: game units per real metre; uniform, no compression
meta.originNote: Chinatown / Financial District edge: Kearny St between California and Sacramento Streets
meta.coverage: South edge just below Oracle Park, Mission Creek and the Caltrain depot; north past Pier 39 and Pier 45 into the Bay; west past Van Ness Ave (City Hall, the Opera House, Ghirardelli Square, Aquatic Park); east into the Bay past the Embarcadero piers and the Bay Bridge anchorage. 696 x 877 u (3.5 x 4.4 km).
meta.terrain: FLAT. San Francisco is steep (Nob Hill 105 m, Russian Hill 90 m, Telegraph Hill 85 m, Rincon Hill 30 m above the Bay); the game ground is flat and the hills are not modelled. Heights are measured from each building's own ground. Streets that really run in tunnels (the Broadway and Stockton tunnels) are plain surface streets here (tunnel: true).
meta.axes: +X = east, -Z = north (true north up), +Y up. Matches the minimap (screen up = -Z).
meta.gridNote: Two street grids meet at Market St and are kept. north_of_market (the Financial District, Chinatown, Nob Hill, North Beach, the Tenderloin, Civic Center, Fisherman's Wharf): avenues bear 351 deg (9 deg west of north), cross streets 81 deg; street-aligned rot about 0.157. soma (South of Market, Rincon Hill, South Beach, Mission Bay): Market St and the streets parallel to it bear 45 deg, the numbered streets 135 deg; rot about +-0.785. waterfront: the piers follow the curve of the Embarcadero seawall. Columbus Avenue cuts the north grid on a diagonal. Landmark front = compass point of frontBearing (deg clockwise from north) and frontDir = the world (x, z) unit vector; grid = the landmark's grid.
meta.rotNote: All rot values are three.js rotation.y (radians). An object rotated by rot has its local +X axis pointing along (cos rot, -sin rot) in world (x, z). Building w is along local X, d along local Z: footprints on the rotated grids are oriented rects (OBB), not axis-aligned. rot is folded into (-pi/4, pi/4].
meta.footprintNote: Footprints are CCW viewed from above (CCW in (x, -z)), open rings (first vertex not repeated). For THREE.Shape use (x, -z) then rotateX(-PI/2).
meta.heightNote: height / eaveHeight are game units (metres x 0.2). Landmarks: heightMetres = top of the structure incl. spires and masts; eaveMetres = main roof, or where the crown / spire begins; dataRoofMetres = the OSM height of the matched footprint. Buildings: heightMetres = the OpenStreetMap height tag (in San Francisco mostly the city's 2010-11 LiDAR roof heights), else the height of the tallest building:part, else building:levels x 3.4 + 1.5, else the DataSF Building Footprints hgt_median_m of the footprint under the building, else the nine nearest neighbours' median; a merged block mass takes the area-weighted height and keeps heightMaxMetres.
meta.mergeNote: Touching buildings (so always inside one street block) under 60 m within 1.8x of each other in height are merged while their union fills at least 62% of its rectangle and no side passes 110 m; slivers under 700 m2 then fold into the nearest-height touching neighbour (2.6x, fill 45%). San Francisco's rows of 25 ft house lots become block-face rows this way. A tower standing on a podium in the data (building:part) is split into the tower (its own entry) and the podium (podiumOf = the tower's id). footprint = the outline; cx/cz/w/d/rot = its oriented rectangle (what the kit fills); phoneSkip = small low structures that touch no street.
meta.buildingFields: osm = the OpenStreetMap way / relation of the outline (the largest member of a merged row); onPier = stands on a pier deck or over the Bay (keep it, do not drop it as in-water); zone = financial_district / chinatown / north_beach / telegraph_hill / fishermans_wharf / russian_hill / nob_hill / union_square / tenderloin / civic_center / soma / south_beach / embarcadero / rincon_hill / mission_bay; style (generic only; landmark footprints carry landmark = the id and no style) = victorian (2-4 storey bay-windowed wood row houses and flats), brick (historic brick / terracotta blocks 1906-1930), warehouse (pier sheds, SoMa brick-and-timber warehouses), lowrise (< 15 m commercial), midrise (15-60 m offices / hotels), apartment (15-60 m residential), glassslab (60-120 m), glasstower (120 m and more); frontage = avenue (faces a north-south or numbered street) / street; merged = number of outlines in the mass.
meta.projection: equirectangular about origin: x = (lon-lon0)*88078.7*scale, z = -(lat-lat0)*110992.5*scale (WGS84 metres per degree at lat0)
meta.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), BBBike extract of San Francisco (download.bbbike.org, snapshot 2026-11-14): coastline, piers, roads, parks, paths, bridges, rail, cable-car and ferry routes, building outlines, names, heights and building parts, park trees. City and County of San Francisco open data (DataSF, data.sfgov.org, PDDL): Building Footprints (ynuv-fyni, LiDAR heights) and Street Tree List (tkzw-k3nq). Terrain tiles (Mapzen / AWS Open Data terrarium; USGS 3DEP, SRTM) for the surround's ground heights. Landmark heights: CTBUH / Skyscraper Center and Wikipedia figures as given in tools/sf/SPEC.md.
meta.generator: tools/sf/cartographer/ (extract_osm.py, fetch_datasf.py, prep.py, gen_layout.py, gen_layout2.py, landmarks.py, gen_detail.py, gen_surround.py, gen_trees.py, validate.py, preview.py)
meta.gridsNote: degrees WEST of north of each grid's north-south streets (as Seattle's grids)
meta.gridRotationNote: degrees clockwise of north of the dominant (north-of-Market) grid: its avenues bear 351 deg, i.e. 9 deg anticlockwise

droppedLandmarks.reason: the Pier 3 shed is not in the data as its own building (only the pier deck and the bulkhead / Pier 1 1/2 buildings)

meta.bayExtension: The play box runs north of the city (z < -444.0) over open Bay to z = -880.0 so Alcatraz and the Golden Gate Bridge are in play. Both are at true size; the bridge is moved in from 6.5 km west (it springs from the Aquatic Park shore at the north-west corner), Alcatraz about 1 km east of its true spot. tools/sf/extend_bay.py

minimap.note: District names for the minimap (centres) and the tier-A landmarks to mark on it; the map itself draws from roads / water / parks / buildings. Screen up = -Z (north).

landmarks.name: Transamerica Pyramid
landmarks.desc: William Pereira's 1972 pyramid, 260 m: a four-sided spike of white crushed-quartz precast concrete panels with rows of small square windows, tapering from a 53 m square base to a point. Two vertical 'wings' (the lift shaft on the east face, the stair and smoke tower on the west) stand proud of the upper 19 floors, and the top 64 m is a hollow aluminium-louvred spire with a beacon. The base stands on a forest of criss-crossing diagonal concrete columns two storeys high; a redwood grove fills the east half of the block.

landmarks.name: Salesforce Tower
landmarks.desc: Pelli Clarke Pelli's 2018 tower, 326 m, the tallest in the city: a slender rounded-square obelisk of clear glass wrapped in horizontal white metal sunshade fins, tapering gently and ending in a hollow perforated-aluminium crown about 30 m high that carries a wraparound LED artwork at night. The corners are soft curves; the base opens to Mission St and the transit center's rooftop park.

landmarks.name: 555 California Street
landmarks.desc: The 1969 Bank of America Center, 237 m: a massive dark slab clad in polished carnelian (red-brown) granite, its whole facade folded into thousands of faceted bay windows of bronze-tinted glass that run in saw-tooth vertical ribs. The top steps back irregularly like a quartz crystal. A dark granite plaza on California St holds the black 'Banker's Heart' sculpture.

landmarks.name: 181 Fremont
landmarks.desc: The 2018 mixed-use tower, 245 m to the spire tip: a slender, slightly folded shaft of blue-grey glass with a white steel exoskeleton of giant diagonal mega-braces zig-zagging up each face. The facades crease inward along the braces; the top tapers to an asymmetric peak with a thin spire.

landmarks.name: Millennium Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2009 condominium tower, 197 m: a soft-cornered slab of blue-grey glass with faint horizontal spandrel bands and a subtly faceted, bowed profile, flat roof. A 12-storey glass mid-rise wing stands beside it on Mission St. (It is the tower famous for sinking and leaning.)

landmarks.name: One Rincon Hill
landmarks.desc: The 2008 South Tower of One Rincon Hill, 184 m, alone on the hilltop beside the Bay Bridge approach: a slim tower of blue-green glass with one long curved (oval) side and white aluminium fin bands, topped by a canted oval crown band that holds the tuned liquid damper tank and a weather beacon. Townhouse podium of pale concrete at the base.

landmarks.name: One Embarcadero Center
landmarks.desc: One Embarcadero Center (1971, 173 m), John Portman's first tower: a very thin slab of pale ribbed precast concrete stepped back in vertical slices at both ends so the plan narrows like staggered dominoes, narrow vertical window strips between closely spaced fins. It stands on a three-storey podium of shops with open walkways, spiral stairs and footbridges linking all four blocks.

landmarks.name: Two Embarcadero Center
landmarks.desc: Two Embarcadero Center (1974, 126 m): the shorter twin of the same thin, stepped slab of pale precast concrete ribs and narrow window strips on the three-storey retail podium with its bridges across the streets.

landmarks.name: Three Embarcadero Center
landmarks.desc: Three Embarcadero Center (1977, 126 m): thin stepped slab of pale ribbed precast concrete like its neighbours, on the three-storey podium of shops and open terraces.

landmarks.name: Four Embarcadero Center
landmarks.desc: Four Embarcadero Center (1982, 174 m), the east end of the complex beside the Hyatt Regency: the tallest of the four thin, stepped pale concrete slabs with vertical ribs, on the three-storey podium facing Embarcadero Plaza.

landmarks.name: 345 California Center
landmarks.desc: The 1986 345 California Center, 212 m, in the middle of a block behind older bank buildings: a slim tower faced in grey-pink granite and silver-blue glass with chamfered, notched corners. The top eleven floors (a hotel) split into two glass towers turned 45 degrees and joined by glazed skybridges, each crowned by an angled flagpole-like spire.

landmarks.name: 101 California Street
landmarks.desc: Philip Johnson's 1982 tower, 183 m: a faceted cylinder of silver-grey glass and granite ribs (a serrated 'sawtooth' drum with about 100 small facets) rising from a seven-storey sloping glass atrium wedge at its foot, on a triangular stepped granite plaza with planters where California St meets Market St.

landmarks.name: 44 Montgomery
landmarks.desc: The 1967 former Wells Fargo headquarters, 172 m: a plain International Style slab, its long faces a tight grid of white aluminium vertical mullions over dark glass, flat top, on a recessed glass lobby at Montgomery and Market.

landmarks.name: One Market Plaza (Spear Tower)
landmarks.desc: The Spear Tower of One Market Plaza (1976, 172 m): a dark bronze-brown slab with closely spaced vertical precast fins and a serrated plan, flat top. It rises behind the 1916 Southern Pacific headquarters, an eleven-storey red-brick and terra cotta block facing the foot of Market St; a lower twin (Steuart Tower) stands to the south-east.

landmarks.name: 50 Fremont Center
landmarks.desc: The 1985 50 Fremont Center, 183 m: a square tower of pale grey-pink granite with a regular grid of punched square windows, the corners notched, the top stepping back in several tiers to a small square crown.

landmarks.name: One Post (McKesson Plaza)
landmarks.desc: One Post / McKesson Plaza (1969, 161 m): a square bronze-coloured tower, bronze-tinted glass between dark vertical ribs, with chamfered corners and a slight flare at the base, standing over the sunken plaza of the Montgomery St station where Post meets Market.

landmarks.name: Park Tower at Transbay
landmarks.desc: The 2018 Park Tower at Transbay, 184 m: a clear glass office tower with crisp white horizontal fins, cut by three stacked double-height notches (sky decks with trees) that step round its corners, flat top.

landmarks.name: 555 Mission Street
landmarks.desc: The 2008 office tower, 149 m: a clean slab of pale green glass, the east and west faces leaning out very slightly, with a tall glass-fin crown and a small plaza of sculptures on Mission St.

landmarks.name: First Market Tower (525 Market)
landmarks.desc: First Market Tower (1973, 161 m): a broad, dark 1970s slab, charcoal precast piers and bronze glass in a strict vertical grid, flat roof, set back from Market St behind a plaza.

landmarks.name: One Sansome
landmarks.desc: One Sansome / Citigroup Center (1984, 168 m): a pale grey-white stone tower with a grid of square windows and rounded bay corners, rising beside the roofless marble banking hall of the 1910 Anglo & London Paris National Bank, kept as an open conservatory at the corner of Sutter and Sansome.

landmarks.name: The Infinity (Tower II, the taller)
landmarks.desc: The Infinity, Tower II (2009, 137 m, 42 storeys): the taller of the two curved clover-plan condominium towers, sea-green glass in smooth unbroken bands with white floor edges, flat top; low curved mid-rise blocks sit between the towers.

landmarks.name: The Infinity (Tower I)
landmarks.desc: The Infinity, Tower I (2008, about 110 m, 37 storeys): a clover-leaf plan tower with every corner a full curve, wrapped in continuous bands of green-tinted glass and thin white slab edges.

landmarks.name: Lumina
landmarks.desc: Lumina, Tower I (2015, 122 m): the sister of the Infinity one block inland: a curving, lozenge-plan condominium tower of pale blue-green glass with rounded ends and white horizontal bands, beside a shorter twin.

landmarks.name: Russ Building
landmarks.desc: The 1927 Russ Building, 133 m, 'the city's first skyscraper': a neo-Gothic E-shaped block of pale cream-grey terra cotta with strong vertical piers, stepping back in tiers to a central tower with Gothic tracery, finials and a flagpole. Deep light courts open to Montgomery St.

landmarks.name: 140 New Montgomery (PacBell Building)
landmarks.desc: Timothy Pflueger's 1925 Pacific Telephone building, 133 m: an Art Deco / neo-Gothic L-plan tower of speckled grey-white terra cotta, soaring unbroken piers that end in a stepped crown of pinnacles, with eight great terra cotta eagles perched on the top corners. Dark recessed spandrels, ornate black-and-gold lobby entrance on New Montgomery St.

landmarks.name: Shell Building
landmarks.desc: The 1929 Shell Building, 115 m: a slender Art Deco tower of rusticated sepia-brown terra cotta, vertical piers rising to a stepped crown decorated with abstract shell forms, once floodlit in gold.

landmarks.name: Hobart Building
landmarks.desc: Willis Polk's 1914 Hobart Building, 87 m: a narrow, ornate cream terra cotta tower with an idiosyncratic oval-ended top, Baroque sculpted cornices and a hipped green-copper cap; its flat, bare south flank (exposed when a neighbour was pulled down) faces Market St.

landmarks.name: Hilton Union Square Tower
landmarks.desc: Hilton San Francisco Union Square, the 1971 tower, 150 m (46 storeys): a pale concrete hotel slab with a grid of windows between slim vertical ribs and a glazed round-cornered sky lounge on top, rising from the full-block Hilton complex in the Tenderloin (with a second, 1987 tower and the 1964 block round a courtyard).

landmarks.name: Marriott Marquis
landmarks.desc: The 1989 Marriott Marquis, 133 m, 'the jukebox': a broad stepped hotel tower of pale pink-beige precast and silver mirror glass, its top a symmetrical pile of fan-shaped mirrored-glass arches and quarter-circles like a Wurlitzer jukebox, with a great arched window to the View Lounge.

landmarks.name: InterContinental San Francisco
landmarks.desc: The 2008 InterContinental, 104 m: a slim slab of translucent pale blue-turquoise glass, flat and unmodelled, on a low podium beside Moscone West at 5th and Howard.

landmarks.name: Four Seasons (757 Market)
landmarks.desc: The 2001 Four Seasons hotel and residences, 121 m: a calm grey stone-and-glass tower with rounded glass corner bays, set back from Market St behind a lower shop block.

landmarks.name: St. Regis Museum Tower
landmarks.desc: The 2005 St. Regis Museum Tower, 148 m: a slender tower of pale precast concrete and glass with a grid of square windows and a glazed corner, standing over the 1907 brick Williams Building and the Museum of the African Diaspora at 3rd and Mission, next to SFMOMA.

landmarks.name: Westin St. Francis
landmarks.desc: The Westin St. Francis on the west side of Union Square: the 1904-13 block of grey Colusa sandstone, twelve storeys with three (later four) projecting wings divided by deep light courts, a heavy cornice and a row of flags over the Powell St cable-car line; behind it the 1972 tower, 120 m, a pale concrete slab with five glass capsule lifts running up its outside face.

landmarks.name: Fairmont Hotel
landmarks.desc: The Fairmont on top of Nob Hill: the 1907 Beaux-Arts palace of white-cream terra cotta and granite, seven storeys, with a columned porte-cochere and a row of flags on Mason St and a roof garden; at its north-east corner the 1961 tower, 99 m, a plain pale slab with an external glass lift to the former Crown Room.

landmarks.name: Mark Hopkins Hotel
landmarks.desc: The 1926 Mark Hopkins Hotel, 93 m, on the crest of Nob Hill: a central tower with two splayed wings round a forecourt, buff brick and cream terra cotta in a French chateau / Spanish Renaissance manner, a steep hipped roof with finials, and the glass-walled Top of the Mark lounge on the 19th floor.

landmarks.name: Hyatt Regency Embarcadero
landmarks.desc: John Portman's 1973 Hyatt Regency, 74 m: a triangular wedge of pale ribbed concrete whose north face steps back floor by floor in a long slope of balconies (the famous 17-storey atrium is inside), with a low drum of the old revolving restaurant on the roof. It closes the east end of Embarcadero Center at the foot of Market and California Streets.

landmarks.name: San Francisco Federal Building
landmarks.desc: Morphosis' 2007 Federal Building, 71 m: a very thin 18-storey slab only 20 m deep. The south-east face is draped in a folded scrim of perforated stainless steel that rides up over the roof and stops short in mid-air; the north-west face has green glass fins; a three-storey void (sky garden) is cut through the slab. A low annex and a plaza on 7th St.

landmarks.name: Phillip Burton Federal Building
landmarks.desc: The 1964 Phillip Burton Federal Building and Courthouse, 95 m: a broad 21-storey International Style slab, a uniform grid of pale precast concrete and dark glass, filling a block of Golden Gate Avenue above a bare plaza.

landmarks.name: Fox Plaza
landmarks.desc: Fox Plaza (1966, 108 m), on the site of the Fox Theatre at Market and Polk: a plain 29-storey slab, beige precast with horizontal window bands, offices below and apartments with balconies above.

landmarks.name: Sentinel Building (Columbus Tower)
landmarks.desc: The 1907 Sentinel Building (Columbus Tower), 30 m: a small eight-storey flatiron at the sharp corner of Columbus Avenue and Kearny St, clad in white tile and copper weathered to pale green, with projecting bay windows up both sides, a rounded prow and a little domed cupola on top. The Transamerica Pyramid rises directly behind it.

landmarks.name: Ferry Building
landmarks.desc: A. Page Brown's 1898 Ferry Building at the foot of Market St: a 201 m long, three-storey hall of grey Colusa sandstone on the bulkhead, its west front a continuous arcade of round arches with a skylit nave behind. In the middle rises the 75 m clock tower modelled on the Giralda of Seville, pale grey, with four 6.7 m clock dials, an arcaded belfry and a small cupola with a flagpole.

landmarks.name: Coit Tower
landmarks.desc: The 1933 tower on the summit of Telegraph Hill, 64 m: a slender fluted cylinder of unpainted white reinforced concrete, slightly tapered, with an arcaded observation loggia of round arches and a second ring of openings at the top; a low rectangular base holds the murals. It stands in the pines and cypresses of Pioneer Park.

landmarks.name: San Francisco City Hall
landmarks.desc: Arthur Brown Jr.'s 1915 City Hall, 94 m: a two-block Beaux-Arts palace of grey Sierra granite with Doric colonnades and pedimented centre porticoes on both long fronts, crowned by a tall dome on a colonnaded drum: lead-grey ribbed dome picked out in gold leaf, with a gilded lantern and torch. The east front faces Civic Center Plaza.

landmarks.name: Grace Cathedral
landmarks.desc: The Episcopal cathedral on Nob Hill (1928-64), 75 m to the fleche: French Gothic in exposed pale grey reinforced concrete, modelled on Notre-Dame, with twin square 53 m west towers, a rose window between them, gilded bronze 'Gates of Paradise' doors, flying-buttress-like piers along the nave and a slender lead fleche over the crossing. A broad flight of steps falls east to Taylor St.

landmarks.name: Saints Peter and Paul Church
landmarks.desc: The 1924 Saints Peter and Paul Church on the north side of Washington Square, 58 m: a white Romanesque-revival front with twin slender spires of open arcaded stages, a rose window and a mosaic band with a line of Dante across the facade; cream-white stucco nave behind.

landmarks.name: Old St. Mary's Cathedral
landmarks.desc: Old St. Mary's (1854), the first cathedral of California, at California St and Grant Avenue: a red-brick Gothic Revival church on a granite base with a square central clock tower with battlements, 27 m; under the clock the gilt text 'Son, observe the time and fly from evil'.

landmarks.name: Dragon Gate (Chinatown)
landmarks.desc: The 1970 Dragon Gate across Grant Avenue at Bush St, the entrance to Chinatown: three bays (a wide road arch and two footway arches) of grey stone piers carrying roofs of green glazed tile with upturned eaves, two gold dragons chasing a pearl on the main ridge, fish and dolphins on the corners, and a pair of stone guardian lions at the foot.

landmarks.name: Sing Chong Building
landmarks.desc: The 1908 Sing Chong Building at the north-west corner of California St and Grant Avenue: a four-storey buff and cream brick bazaar with green-and-red painted trim and a corner tower in three diminishing pagoda roofs with upturned eaves and a finial, 22 m: the building that set the look of rebuilt Chinatown, facing the cable cars on California St.

landmarks.name: Old Chinese Telephone Exchange
landmarks.desc: The 1909 Chinese Telephone Exchange on Washington St: a small one-storey pavilion under three tiers of curving green-tiled pagoda roofs with red lacquered columns, gold trim and upturned eaves, about 12 m.

landmarks.name: Oracle Park
landmarks.desc: The Giants' ballpark (2000) on China Basin: a red-brick and green-steel park in the old style, three decks of dark green seats wrapping the infield, a brick arcade and promenade along the right-field wall directly on McCovey Cove (home runs splash into the water), four banks of lights on steel towers, the big scoreboard in centre field, and behind the left-field bleachers a giant old-fashioned baseball glove and a soda-bottle slide. Brick clock towers with pyramid roofs mark the entrances at Willie Mays Plaza.

landmarks.name: Pier 39
landmarks.desc: The 1978 shopping pier, about 300 m long: two storeys of grey weathered-timber sheds, shops and restaurants with shingled gables, balconies and outside stairs round a central boardwalk, flagpoles all along the roofs, a two-level Venetian carousel near the outer end, a marina on both sides, and on the west side the floating docks crowded with sea lions.

landmarks.name: Fisherman's Wharf sign
landmarks.desc: The Fisherman's Wharf sign at Jefferson and Taylor Streets: a round ship's wheel about 6 m across with a red crab in the middle and white lettering round the rim, on a tall post above the crab stands.

landmarks.name: Ghirardelli Square
landmarks.desc: The former chocolate works above Aquatic Park, converted in 1964: a full block of red-brick factory buildings with crenellated parapets round terraced courts and a fountain, the 1916 Clock Tower (modelled on the Chateau de Blois, about 40 m) at the south-east corner, and a giant illuminated roof sign in 4.5 m letters on a steel frame facing the bay.

landmarks.name: Balclutha (Hyde Street Pier)
landmarks.desc: The 1886 Clyde-built square-rigger at the Hyde Street Pier: a three-masted full-rigged steel ship, 92 m overall with the bowsprit, black hull with a white strake and red boot-topping, white deckhouses, buff masts and yards about 44 m high with furled sails and a web of rigging.
landmarks.osm: way/456528981 (Hyde Street Pier; the ship itself is not mapped)

landmarks.name: USS Pampanito and SS Jeremiah O'Brien (Pier 45)
landmarks.desc: The museum ships on the east side of Pier 45: SS Jeremiah O'Brien, a 135 m grey Liberty ship of 1943 with a central island, single funnel, cargo masts and gun tubs, and moored astern of her the black-grey Balao-class submarine USS Pampanito, 95 m, low in the water with her fairwater and deck guns.
landmarks.osm: way/165601339 (USS Pampanito; SS Jeremiah O'Brien placed ahead of her)

landmarks.name: Pier 45 sheds
landmarks.desc: The four long Pier 45 sheds (A to D, 1926) at Fisherman's Wharf: white-painted concrete transit sheds in two rows with shallow gabled roofs and neoclassical arched end facades, home of the fish processors and the Musee Mecanique.

landmarks.name: Aquarium of the Bay
landmarks.desc: The aquarium at the landward end of Pier 39: a two-storey grey timber-clad building with a blue wave-topped entrance and banners on the Embarcadero.

landmarks.name: Exploratorium (Pier 15)
landmarks.desc: The Exploratorium in the 1931 Pier 15 shed: a 250 m long white transit shed with a low gabled roof covered in solar panels running out over the bay, fronted on the Embarcadero by a cream neoclassical bulkhead building with a great central arch.

landmarks.name: James R. Herman Cruise Terminal (Pier 27)
landmarks.desc: The 2014 James R. Herman Cruise Terminal on Pier 27: a long two-storey box of glass and white metal with a folded roof and a projecting gangway gallery, on a broad apron under Telegraph Hill.

landmarks.name: Cupid's Span
landmarks.desc: Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen's 2002 sculpture in Rincon Park: a giant gold bow and red-feathered arrow, 18 m high, the arrow and the middle of the bow buried in the lawn so that the bow arcs like a ship or a suspension bridge against the Bay Bridge.

landmarks.name: Vaillancourt Fountain
landmarks.desc: Armand Vaillancourt's 1971 fountain in Embarcadero Plaza: a 12 m tangle of square precast concrete tubes with a rough, rusty-stained texture, jutting at all angles over a pool with stepping-stone slabs.

landmarks.name: SFMOMA
landmarks.desc: Mario Botta's 1995 museum on 3rd St: stepped symmetrical boxes of red-brown patterned brick, with a black-and-white striped stone cylinder sliced off at an angle (the oculus) rising in the middle; behind and above it Snohetta's 2016 extension, a 60 m slab of rippled white fibre-reinforced panels like fog or bay water.

landmarks.name: Salesforce Transit Center
landmarks.desc: The 2018 transit center, 440 m long and four storeys, bridging First and Fremont Streets: a low undulating hall wrapped in a white perforated aluminium skin with a Penrose pattern, carried on tree-like V-columns, with a 2 ha rooftop park of lawns and trees along its whole length and a bus bridge to the Bay Bridge at the west end.

landmarks.name: Moscone Center
landmarks.desc: Moscone South (rebuilt 2018) on Howard St: a long glass-and-white-steel convention hall front with terraces and footbridges across Howard St to Moscone North; the exhibition halls are underground beneath the roof gardens of Yerba Buena.

landmarks.name: Contemporary Jewish Museum
landmarks.desc: Daniel Libeskind's 2008 museum: the red-brick 1907 Jessie Street power substation with a cream terra cotta cornice, skewered by a tilted cube and a skewed block of shimmering blue steel panels standing on one corner.

landmarks.name: Dewey Monument (Union Square)
landmarks.desc: The 1903 Dewey Monument in the centre of Union Square: a 26 m Corinthian column of pale granite on a square pedestal, topped by a bronze Victory holding a trident and a wreath.

landmarks.name: Emporium dome (Westfield San Francisco Centre)
landmarks.desc: The 1896 Emporium on Market St (now the San Francisco Centre): a grey sandstone Beaux-Arts front with a giant order of columns and a central arch, and behind it the 31 m wide glass-and-steel dome, lifted onto the roof of the new centre.

landmarks.name: Flood Building
landmarks.desc: The 1904 Flood Building at Powell and Market by the cable-car turntable: twelve storeys of grey Colusa sandstone, a flatiron with a rounded corner, a rusticated base, giant-order middle and a heavy cornice.

landmarks.name: Phelan Building
landmarks.desc: The 1908 Phelan Building: an eleven-storey flatiron of glazed cream-white terra cotta filling the point between Market St and O'Farrell St, with a rounded prow and a deep cornice.

landmarks.name: Palace Hotel
landmarks.desc: The 1909 Palace Hotel at Market and New Montgomery: a broad eight-storey block of buff brick with terra cotta trim, roof signs on steel frames, and the glass-roofed Garden Court inside.

landmarks.name: Old San Francisco Mint
landmarks.desc: The 1874 Old Mint, the 'Granite Lady', at 5th and Mission: a severe Greek Revival block of blue-grey sandstone on a granite basement, with a six-column Doric portico and pediment up a broad flight of steps and two tall square chimneys behind.

landmarks.name: War Memorial Opera House
landmarks.desc: The 1932 War Memorial Opera House on Van Ness Avenue opposite City Hall: a Beaux-Arts block of grey granite and terra cotta, a rusticated base, a row of tall arched windows between paired Doric columns, and a mansard roof; the fly tower rises at the back.

landmarks.name: War Memorial Veterans Building
landmarks.desc: The 1932 Veterans Building (Herbst Theatre), the Opera House's near-twin across the memorial court: grey granite and terra cotta, rusticated base, tall arched windows between paired columns, mansard roof.

landmarks.name: Davies Symphony Hall
landmarks.desc: The 1980 Louise M. Davies Symphony Hall: a pale precast concrete hall whose front on Grove St and Van Ness is a great curved wrap of glass lobbies in tiers between concrete fins.

landmarks.name: Asian Art Museum
landmarks.desc: The 1917 former Main Library, since 2003 the Asian Art Museum: a Beaux-Arts block of grey granite on the east side of Civic Center Plaza with a row of arched windows and Ionic columns.

landmarks.name: San Francisco Main Library
landmarks.desc: The 1996 Main Library: a grey granite block that echoes its Beaux-Arts neighbours on the Civic Center side and turns to a modern glass-and-metal facade on Market St, with a round skylit atrium.

landmarks.name: Bill Graham Civic Auditorium
landmarks.desc: The 1915 Exposition Auditorium on the south side of Civic Center Plaza: a broad grey granite Beaux-Arts block with three great arched windows under a canopy and a low hipped roof.

landmarks.name: Cable Car Museum and powerhouse
landmarks.desc: The 1887 / 1907 Washington-Mason car barn and powerhouse: a red-brick block with arched windows and corbelled parapets and a tall square brick chimney, where the great winding wheels drive all the cable-car lines.

landmarks.name: Pacific-Union Club (Flood Mansion)
landmarks.desc: The 1886 James C. Flood mansion, the only Nob Hill palace to survive 1906: a dark Connecticut brownstone Italianate block of two tall storeys with a columned porch, behind a bronze fence, on California St opposite the Fairmont.

landmarks.name: San Francisco Caltrain station (4th and King)
landmarks.desc: The Caltrain terminus at 4th and King Streets: a low single-storey 1970s station of tan concrete and glass with a flat canopy at the head of twelve stub tracks and platforms.

landmarks.name: Lefty O'Doul (Third Street) Bridge
landmarks.desc: The 1933 Lefty O'Doul Bridge by Joseph Strauss: a heel-trunnion bascule carrying 3rd St over the mouth of Mission Creek beside the ballpark: riveted grey-green steel through trusses with a great overhead concrete counterweight on the north tower.

landmarks.name: Pier 1
landmarks.desc: One of the Embarcadero's numbered finger piers (1910s-30s): a cream-white neoclassical bulkhead building on the roadway with a big central arch and the pier number in the pediment, and behind it a long low transit shed with a shallow gabled roof running out over the bay on piles.

landmarks.name: Golden Gate Bridge
landmarks.desc: The 1937 suspension bridge in International Orange: two 227 m Art Deco towers with stepped portal struts, a 1,280 m main span between them, the deck 67 m over the water, main cables in a long catenary and close-set suspender ropes, the steel arch over Fort Point at the south end. Moved in from the west so it is in play: it runs north from the Aquatic Park shore to Marin.

landmarks.name: Alcatraz Island
landmarks.desc: The Rock: a 510 m tan sandstone island with cliffs, the long pale cellhouse on its crown, the lighthouse, the water tower, the ruined warden's house, the dock and guard tower on the east side and the industries building at the north-west end. Stands in the Bay off Fisherman's Wharf (about 1 km east of its true spot).

player.note: Rises from San Francisco Bay off the Embarcadero, north-east of the Ferry Building beyond the ends of Piers 1 to 7, and wades south-west: the Ferry Building clock tower stands dead ahead with the four Embarcadero Center slabs and the Financial District behind it, the Transamerica Pyramid to the right, Salesforce Tower and the Bay Bridge anchorage to the left. rot = rotation.y that turns a +Z-forward model to face the facing vector.

ring.note: Title Match ring in low-rise South of Market at about 37.7787, -122.4085: the blocks of one- to four-storey brick-and-timber warehouses, workshops and car parks; the level leaves out the blocks inside venueBox in that mode. The downtown skyline (Salesforce Tower, 181 Fremont, the Marriott 'jukebox', the PacBell Building) rises to the north-east, City Hall's dome to the west. venueBox [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ] = the Chicago venue x -58..+48, z -78..+78 with both grandstands; runwayBox = the entrance runway and gate (x +48..+73); east / west = 0 (nothing pulled in). No landmark centre lies within 46 u on both axes; the box is dry. clearToBuildings = distance from the centre to the first building of 25 m or more in each direction. tallInVenueBox lists generic buildings of 30 m or more whose footprints fall in the box (not built in that mode); freewayInVenueBox = length (u) of elevated I-80 inside the box.
